newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt trading volume over $1.4 trln in Q2 -EMTA.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt trading volume over $1.4 trln in Q2 -EMTA.

text.p: Trading volume in emerging markets debt instruments totaled more than $1.4 trillion in second quarter 1997, down from $1.6 trillion in the first quarter, an Emerging Markets Trade Association report said.
An influx of new money at the beginning of the year tends to boost first quarter figures, explained Paul Masco, EMTA vice chair and a managing director at Salomon Brothers.
"In addition, speculation about interest rates in February and March made the market more volatile in the first quarter," Masco said.

EMTA reported $601 billion of Brady bond trading last quarter, down from $671 billion in the first quarter. In Eurobonds, $290 billion of turnover was reported, compared with $361 billion in the previous three months.
EMTA reported turnover of $369 billion in local markets instruments, $93 billion in debt options and $60 billion in loan transactions.
Brazilian debt instruments remained the most commonly traded, with $436 billion changing hands. Brazil's C bond again led the way among individual instruments, with $155 billion traded.
Argentina's debt was the second-most commonly traded, with $298 billion, and Mexico placed third, with $229 billion.
Trading in Russian debt surged 28 percent to $132 billion last quarter, EMTA said.
U.S. financial institutions handled 60 percent of second quarter trading, a breakdown unchanged from the prior quarter, it said.
